taxonomy-pdf-targeted.json.cacheProtocol: Scripts/build-cache.sh exclusive lease and EXIT trap; GLIFI_VERIFY_KEEP_CACHE=1
nativePDFDiagnostics: CoreGraphics PDF has logged an error. Set environment variable "CG_PDF_VERBOSE" to learn more.

pdf-v2-targeted-green.json.shellScript:
set -euo pipefail
source Scripts/build-cache.sh
task_cache_directory="$(glifi_build_cache_directory)"
trap 'glifi_release_build_cache "$task_cache_directory"' EXIT
glifi_prepare_build_cache "$task_cache_directory" || exit 1
swift test --package-path Packages/GlifiCore --scratch-path "$task_cache_directory/SwiftPM" --jobs 2 --no-parallel --filter 'pdfVision|pdfImporter|pdfOCRExecution|pdfProfileProvenance'

ocr-reimport-persistence-audit.json.scope: Read-only reimport, snapshot identity and persistence review; no storage/source patch or runtime execution

conclusion.currentReimportSemantics: Append-only. A shared SourceID does not replace or hide an earlier revision; both remain active in the project corpus. Binary bytes are content-addressed/deduplicated, not the logical acquisitions.
conclusion.oneExtractionPerRevision: Enforced by bindings; a new profile may create a new acquisition/revision, not a second artifact for an existing revision.

codeEvidence.observation: SourceRevisionID is a UUID-backed opaque identifier, not a hash of the original bytes or OCR profile.
The import factory defaults sourceRevisionID to a new SourceRevisionID; the extraction returns one DTO that restoreDocument binds to that revision.
Source record uses the supplied SourceID and imported revision, points original object to raw SHA path and appends to all current sources.

Descriptor identity includes sourceRevisionIDs, original source record, extractionDigest, complete backendMetadata and backendIdentifier. Different policy/backend remains distinct even if captured text is identical.
Existing extraction declares exactly its own revision; adding another revision preserves this corpus subset and therefore retains the old extraction artifact.
Duplicate source revisions, more than one reserved extraction for one revision, and missing rich extractions fail closed.
The new source adds exactly one prepared extraction, validates the graph/bindings and only then prepares the database generation.
SQLite copies historical source rows and inserts the new revision; primary key is generation/source_revision_id, not SourceID.
Reopen validates/rebuilds the descriptor from persisted payload.extraction, not the current recognizer policy. Canonical bytes and stored metadata are preserved.

regressionsProposed.setup: Use fixed SourceID, two distinct fixed SourceRevisionID values, identical opaque non-PDF raw bytes, identical captured UTF8 text/locations. V1 has legacy backend and no new policy metadata. V2 has explicit new policy/backend metadata. Construct both via restoreDocument so any accidental parser call would fail.
steps: Import V1 under shared SourceID. Save original source record, extraction artifact, descriptor bytes, payload bytes, nodeID and ArtifactID.
Import V2 under the SAME SourceID with the FRESH revision.
Reopen and load importedText for each revision independently.
assertions: Generation advances exactly once for V2; two source records and exactly two reserved artifacts, one per revision.
SourceID equal and contentDigest/objectPath/raw bytes equal; SourceRevisionIDs differ.
V1 source record, artifact, descriptor and payload bytes/IDs remain exactly unchanged.
V2 nodeID, ArtifactID, extractionDigest and backend identity differ, even with identical captured text.
Both captured texts/ranges and source raw digests match expected values after reopen.
V1 metadata remains policy-less and byte-identical; V2 preserves the selected new profile/backend.
No Vision/PDFKit invocation; opaque original cannot be parsed.

regressionsProposed.setup: Reuse V1 SourceRevisionID intentionally for V2 metadata/backend, keeping SourceID and raw bytes equal.
assertions: Import throws a typed GlifiFailure before manifest replacement; no second committed artifact binds that revision.
